subject: golden poison frog
title: This Frog Has Poison for 10 People. Raised in a Zoo, It Has None

scenes.text: This tiny frog carries enough poison to kill about ten people. In a zoo, it's harmless.
The golden poison frog lives in the rainforests of Colombia, and it's only about five centimeters long.
Its skin holds batrachotoxin, one of the most powerful poisons in nature.
But frogs raised in captivity have no detectable toxin at all.
The frog doesn't make the poison itself. It comes from its wild diet, probably tiny beetles.
Take away the bugs, and one of the most poisonous animals on Earth is just a bright yellow frog.

description:
One golden poison frog carries enough batrachotoxin to kill roughly 10 adults, according to estimates reported by the American Museum of Natural History and National Geographic.
Yet frogs raised in captivity have no detectable batrachotoxin: the poison comes from their wild diet, most likely small beetles, though the exact source is still unknown.
What other animal gets its weapon from its food?
first_comment: A similar toxin turned up in New Guinea birds and the beetles they eat, which is why scientists suspect beetles. Would you hold one from a zoo?
